key_insight: Combining AI predictions from radiology Findings and Impressions improved identification of brain metastases compared with either section alone.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline could expand cancer registry surveillance to brain metastases detected after the initial cancer diagnosis; it is not a drug discovery tool.
method: Manually labeled brain/head radiology reports from an Alberta cancer cohort.
Trained separate Bio_ClinicalBERT models on Findings and Impressions, using the higher probability as the report-level prediction.
Validated internally in Alberta and externally in Ontario and British Columbia.
evidence_signal: Trained on 1,879 samples, the model achieved 88.8% sensitivity and 49.9% precision on 1,833 internal-validation reports at a 0.4 threshold; external sensitivity was 91.8% in Ontario and 72.6% in British Columbia.
watch_item: Modest internal precision and variable external sensitivity warrant assessing false-positive review burden and local performance before surveillance deployment.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
